question: A heap of wheat is in the form of a cone of diameter 30 m and height 8 m. How much canvas cloth will be required to just cover the heap (take π = 3.14)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m, Height (h) = 8 m.

Using the Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), the slant height (l) = 17 m.

Canvas required = Curved Surface Area = πrl

⇒ Area = 3.14 × 15 × 17 = 3.14 × 255 = 800.7

**∴ The correct answer is 800.7 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the base of the cone (d) = 30 m

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m

Height of the cone (h) = 8 m

Value of π = 3.14

 

 

 
 
• 
 h = 8 m
 
• 
 r = 15 m
 l = 17 m
 Canvas Area = Curved Surface Area

**Formula Used:**

Slant height of a cone (l) = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cone = πrl

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the slant height (l) of the conical heap:

⇒ l = √(15² + 8²)

⇒ l = √(225 + 64)

⇒ l = √289 = 17 m

⇒ The area of the canvas required to just cover the heap is equal to its Curved Surface Area.

⇒ Canvas required = πrl

⇒ Canvas required = 3.14 × 15 × 17

⇒ Canvas required = 3.14 × 255

⇒ Canvas required = 800.7 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 800.7 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes both the curved surface and the flat circular base: TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder that has the same base radius and height: Volume = (1/3)πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Using standard right-angle triangle triplets such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) helps in quickly finding the missing side lengths in 2D and 3D geometry problems.
